reasoning_traces.think:
The BIC primitive aggregates 18 scalar injury criteria (HIC, BrIC, GAMBIT, HIP) from head-impact kinematics, mapping them to FE-derived brain strain values. This establishes a deterministic mapping from biomechanical input to injury likelihood. The Fast Brain Strain Evaluation primitive bridges sensor data to FE strain estimates, enabling real-time inference. These two primitives form a dual system where BIC provides static criteria and Fast Brain Strain offers dynamic strain estimation. The tractography QC inspector ensures data integrity for downstream processing. Failure modes include sensor noise, model misalignment, and data inconsistency. Dualities arise in how both systems map physical phenomena to scalar metrics, while their failure modes stem from calibration drift and domain shift.
